name: Spastic Tetraplegia-Retinits Pigmentosa-Intellectual Disability Syndrome
aliases: Spastic Tetraplegia with Retinitis Pigmentosa and Intellectual Disability

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Spastic Tetraplegia-Retinits Pigmentosa-Intellectual Disability Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of early-onset spastic tetraplegia with increased muscle tone and hyperreflexia
Clinical and ophthalmological evidence of retinitis pigmentosa including night blindness and peripheral visual field loss
Documented intellectual disability ranging from moderate to severe
Brain MRI showing nonspecific white matter changes or cerebral atrophy
Identification of pathogenic variants in associated genes if known

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (spastic tetraplegia, retinitis pigmentosa, and intellectual disability) must be present for diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation may support diagnosis but is not mandatory due to limited gene identification.

laboratory: Possible mild elevation of muscle enzymes secondary to spasticity
imaging: Brain MRI showing nonspecific white matter abnormalities or cerebral atrophy
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing retinal degeneration
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes associated with hereditary spastic paraplegia or retinal dystrophies if identified
other: Electromyography (EMG) may show upper motor neuron pattern
Visual field testing confirming peripheral constriction

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly lower limb spasticity rather than tetraplegia
Progressive neurodegeneration with seizures and vision loss
Onset typically in childhood with rapid progression

redFlags: Rapid progression of visual loss leading to blindness
Early onset severe spastic tetraplegia with failure to achieve motor milestones
references: Orphanet: Spastic tetraplegia-retinitis pigmentosa-intellectual disability syndrome (ORPHA:3011)
